title: Recovered fixed-rate geometric formation: independent recomputation and small-N replay
what: RECOVERED CODEX SCIENCE (2026-09-26), WORKED COMPUTATION (independent run 1 of 2). SETTING: on 2026-09-21 a Codex campaign ran a declared fixed-rate follow-up of the geometric record-formation process: periodic cubic lattices N = 16, 32, 64, 128, slide rate kappa = 1, paired-birth rates beta = 0.1, 1, 10, 256 seeded histories per cell (64 at N = 128), 2,496 in all, each from empty to its first complete matching with plaquette rate nu = 0. It was never published: open PR #8589 proves the slow-birth regime and states that the fixed-rate Monte Carlo follow-up remains outside it. Everything that survives is in probes/work/worktree-sweep-20260926/codex-sync-2026-09-21-second/geometric-fixed-rate-formation/: assessment/ (protocol, analysis plan, pre-data correction, author assessment), source/ (geometric_partner_growth.cpp and the run and analysis scripts), results/ (RESULTS.json, TABLE.md, PER_HISTORY.json), verification/ (source and production reviews), run/ (manifest with every seed). The raw trajectories were deleted. The original production check reproduced the 144 point estimates and standard errors from saved sufficient statistics and decoded 24 endpoints; it did not replay trajectories, decode the other 2,472 endpoints, or rerun the bootstrap quantiles. TASK: (1) From assessment/ alone, write your own simulator of the declared process. Do not reuse or translate source/geometric_partner_growth.cpp; read it only after your numbers are fixed, then record any convention difference. Run at least N = 16 at all three beta and N = 32 at beta = 1 and 10 (add N = 32, beta = 0.1 if the budget allows), at least 64 histories per cell with your own seeds. Compute S_1, W, W/S_1, S_4/S_1, mean T/V, slides per site and the fraction of sites with more than one birth, with whole-history bootstrap intervals, and compare with results/TABLE.md cell by cell. (2) With your own code, recompute all 144 point estimates, standard errors and percentile bootstrap intervals (10,000 whole-history resamples; agreement within bootstrap Monte Carlo error suffices) for all 12 cells from results/PER_HISTORY.json, and compare with results/RESULTS.json. HIT: a replayed cell that disagrees with the saved table beyond both sampling errors (state the size of the discrepancy), or a RESULTS.json value your recomputation from PER_HISTORY.json does not reproduce. Keep to one process with BLAS threads = 1, stay under two CPU-hours and 2 GB of memory; this machine froze under parallel numeric load. Agreement is a valid result. Neither agreement nor disagreement turns these finite runs into a theorem or a physical claim; say what your run covers and what it does not. Deliver probes/work/compute/recovered-fixed-rate-geometric-formation/<worker>/run.py and RESULT.md; run.py prints a SUMMARY: line and one HIT: line per discrepancy. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/compute/recovered-fixed-rate-geometric-formation/<worker>/run.py", then python3 probes/claim.py finish <unit>.

title: Recovered dimer-routed colour-wave screen: pending aggregate check and small-N replay
what: RECOVERED CODEX SCIENCE (2026-09-26), WORKED COMPUTATION (independent run 1 of 2). SETTING: on 2026-09-21 a Codex campaign ran a finite-size screen of record-colour waves under dimer-routed record transport: 960 histories on periodic cubic lattices N = 16, 32, 64, 128 (256, 128, 64, 32 histories per geometry) for two frozen full matchings (maximal winding along the first axis; an irregular matching made from a columnar one by seeded plaquette proposals), whole-pair exchange with gamma = 1, k0 = 1.1, fixed geometry, independent uniform fourteen-colour initial keys. For each of the three positive fundamental axis modes it recorded four statistics against the conditional Euler propagator (targets at t = 7/8: error 0, transverse 0, signed cross 1, longitudinal 1; at t = 7/4: 0, -1, 0, 1). A declared N = 256 follow-up completed 10 of its 16 histories before its deadline (2 failed, 4 not started). The asymptotic statements under test are in open PRs #8600 and #8604; these finite runs were never published. Everything that survives is in probes/work/worktree-sweep-20260926/codex-sync-2026-09-21-second/dimer-routed-dynamic-screen/ and probes/work/worktree-sweep-20260926/codex-sync-2026-09-21-second/dimer-routed-256-followup/: assessment/ (protocol, the construction note DIMER_ROUTED_RECORD_TRANSPORT.md, assessment or analysis plan), source/ (dimer_routed_dynamics.cpp and scripts), results/ (RESULTS.json, PER_HISTORY.json), verification/, run/ (manifest with every seed; run/frozen_sources/ holds the exact versions each run used). Trajectories and endpoint states were deleted. The original independent check reconstructed 16 selected endpoints and two small event histories; the screen's assessment records that a separate aggregate check was still pending. TASK: (1) The pending aggregate check. With your own code, recompute every aggregate in dimer-routed-dynamic-screen/results/RESULTS.json (all modes, times and components, per geometry and size) and its whole-history percentile bootstrap intervals (10,000 resamples; agreement within bootstrap Monte Carlo error suffices) from results/PER_HISTORY.json, and recompute the censored N = 256 descriptive summary in dimer-routed-256-followup/results/ the same way. (2) From assessment/ and run/frozen_sources/ protocol text alone, write your own simulator of the declared dynamics; do not reuse or translate the saved C++ until your numbers are fixed. Build the winding matching yourself; for the irregular one either regenerate it with the saved setup script and the manifest seed (check its hash against the run/geometry receipts) or build your own per the protocol and compare only qualitatively. Run N = 16 and N = 32 for both geometries with your own seeds, at least 64 histories per cell, and compare the four statistics at t = 7/8 and t = 7/4 with the saved values. HIT: an aggregate your recomputation does not reproduce, or a replayed cell that disagrees with the saved values beyond both sampling errors. Keep to one process with BLAS threads = 1, stay under two CPU-hours and 2 GB of memory; this machine froze under parallel numeric load. Agreement is a valid result. Neither agreement nor disagreement turns these finite runs into a theorem or a physical claim; say what your run covers and what it does not. Deliver probes/work/compute/recovered-dimer-routed-color-waves/<worker>/run.py and RESULT.md; run.py prints a SUMMARY: line and one HIT: line per discrepancy. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/compute/recovered-dimer-routed-color-waves/<worker>/run.py", then python3 probes/claim.py finish <unit>.
